header.userPrompt:
Add Grok Build (`grok`, xAI's coding-agent CLI) as a sixth orca backend: a new `grok/` module (`orca-grok`, package `orca.tools.grok`, `BackendTag.Grok`, settings harness name `grok`), wired through every registration touchpoint so `codingAgent = grok` / `grok:<model>` works in settings files, flows (`grok` accessor), the shell (`orca continue`, flow-authoring slug, wizard) and the enforcement table.

The design is already researched — follow these committed documents rather than re-deriving it:
- `INTEGRATE_GROK_BUILD.md` — the grok-specific design: invocation, the reuse of claude's stream-json decoding, ClientClaimed sessions, the tool-enforcement tier mapping (including the empty `--tools` trap), `--json-schema` handling, `ask_user` over MCP via a temp `--agent` file, models/cheap tier, the proposed enforcement row, an implementation sketch, and a list of open questions.
- `HARNESS_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md` — the AgentBackend/LineDecoder contract and the full list of registration touchpoints outside the module (section 7) and testing expectations (section 8).
- `docs/research/harness-integration/fixtures/grok-*.jsonl` — real grok transcripts recorded while probing (see the README there); use them as decoder test fixtures.

Key decisions to honour:
- Extract claude's stream-json decoding (`InboundMessage`, `ContentBlock`, `StreamEventPayload`, the decoder fold) into a shared, parameterized decoder in `tools` that both claude and grok instantiate; claude's behaviour and tests must stay green. Handle the grok differences listed in the doc's section 3 (ask_user echo via `use_tool`/`orca__ask_user`, `errors[]` in failure messages, grok's refusal texts → `ToolDenied`, `"unknown"` model → None, all-zero usage).
- Every read-only / no-tools argv must render a non-empty `--tools` of real tool names; pin that with tests.
- `Full, Only(_)` is classified `Ignored` (the doc's option B).
- Regenerate the AGENTS.md enforcement table via `EnforcementTableTest` and update the hand-maintained NetworkOnly grant list, README and CONTRIBUTING mentions as the guide's section 7 lists.

A logged-in `grok` CLI (1.0.41) is on PATH in this environment. Use it to settle the doc's open questions where that is cheap (section 11: `--agent` side effects on the system prompt, `server/discover` against orca's own `McpHost`, whether a failed first turn leaves `chat_history.jsonl`, `ask_user_question` in headless mode, resume under a stricter tier), always with `-m grok-4.7-build-fast` and short prompts — live grok calls cost real money, keep them to a handful. Record what you verified back into `INTEGRATE_GROK_BUILD.md` (mark items verified with CLI version and date). Add a gated `GrokIntegrationTest` (`ORCA_INTEGRATION=1`) mirroring the other backends' integration suites, and run it once at the end.

Do not push, open PRs, or change remotes. Do not add pricing rows with guessed rates; if `DefaultModelsPricedTest` needs a row, leave a clearly marked TODO in the test instead of inventing numbers.

tasks.title: Extract claude's stream-json decoding into a shared, dialect-parameterized decoder in tools
Add the grok-needed knobs to the shared stream-json decoder
tasks.description:
Extend `MessagesJsonDecoder`, `InboundMessage` and `MessagesJsonDialect` with the generic hooks grok needs, keeping claude's behaviour identical:
1. Decode `result.errors: List[String]` (absent means Nil) into `InboundMessage.Result`, and include it in the `Settled.Failed` message and in the displayed error when the body is empty. The fixture shape is `"errors":["Couldn't set model 'nope-model': …"]` or `["cancelled"]`. Claude never sends the field, so this can be unconditional; still check that claude's error texts are unchanged when it is absent.
2. A dialect-controlled model normalisation, applied in `turnModel` to both `result.model` and `init.model`. Grok maps `"unknown"` to None; claude is the identity.
3. A dialect-controlled "all-zero usage means unobserved" policy. When every token bucket and the cost are zero, the success path reports the usage as unobserved, and the failure path settles `TurnDebit.Unobserved` instead of `Observed(zeros)`. Check how `Usage`, `Usage.empty` and `TurnDebit` express "no usage" and pick the idiomatic shape. Default is off for claude.
4. `ContentBlock.parse` must keep treating unknown block types (`server_tool_use`, `web_search_tool_result`) as `Unknown`, and extra fields such as `server_tool_use` inside usage must not break `ResultWire` parsing. Add tests with inline lines.

If you add the optional "suppress assistant prose on structured turns" behaviour from design-doc §3.3, gate it behind a dialect flag defaulting to off. Otherwise skip it.

Tests go in tools, using synthetic NDJSON lines and a test dialect, plus `TurnEventConformance.assertGrammar`. Acceptance: `sbt tools/test claude/test` is green.

tasks.title: Probe grok's open questions with the live CLI and record the results
tasks.description:
Docs and probes only, no Scala. Settle the cheap items of `INTEGRATE_GROK_BUILD.md` §11 using the installed `grok` (check `grok --version`; expect 1.0.41). Use `-m grok-4.7-build-fast`, one-line prompts and scratch git repos under `/tmp`, and keep it to about 6 live model calls in total. Items:
1. `--agent` side effects. Compare a plain turn's `$GROK_HOME/sessions/<urlencoded realpath>/<id>/system_prompt.txt` with one run under a temp `--agent` file (frontmatter `prompt_mode: full`, `model: inherit`, `agents_md: true`, and an `mcpServers` list pointing at an unreachable port is fine). Also confirm that `--rules` text still appears.
2. Does a turn that fails before the model runs (e.g. `-m nope-model --session-id <uuid>`) leave `chat_history.jsonl` behind? If so, note whether it is empty and what the probe should require.
3. Is `ask_user_question` listed in init `tools` in headless mode, and what does disallowing it look like? Don't burn a call trying to make the model use it unless it is cheap.
4. Resume under a stricter tier: create a session with `--always-approve`, then `--resume` it with `--tools read_file,grep,list_dir --disallowed-tools search_tool,use_tool --no-subagents` and ask it to write a file. Check the filesystem and the init `tools` list.
5. Free checks via `--help` only: `--no-auto-update`, `--no-subagents`, `--verbatim`, and whether `--cwd` exists.

Do NOT probe `server/discover` here; that happens against orca's `McpHost` in the integration-test task.

Update `INTEGRATE_GROK_BUILD.md`: mark each settled item **[verified grok 1.0.41, 2026-09-27, Linux]** in the §1 matrix, §4, §5 notes, §6 and §11, and state concrete consequences for the implementation (e.g. "probe must also require non-empty history", "always disallow ask_user_question on autonomous turns"). Optionally save any new transcript you rely on under `docs/research/harness-integration/fixtures/` and add it to that README table.

tasks.title: Create the grok module with GrokModels, GrokArgs (tier wiring + enforcement cells) and the grok dialect
tasks.description:
This task adds no BackendTag yet, so nothing outside the module changes except `build.sbt`. There, add `lazy val grok = (project in file("grok")).dependsOn(tools, tools % "test->test")` with `commonSettings`, `name := "orca-grok"` and osLib/jsoniter/jsoniterMacros, and add it to the root `.aggregate(...)`. Do not add it to runner yet. In `grok/src/main/scala/orca/tools/grok/`: - `GrokModels`: `Default = Model("grok-4.7")`, `BuildFast = Model("grok-4.7-build-fast")`. - `GrokArgs` (`private[grok]`), following design-doc §5 and §10 and the probe results already in the doc. It needs `final case class Wiring(args: Seq[String], cell: EnforcementCell)` and `def wiring(tools: ToolSet, autoApprove: AutoApprove, mcp: Boolean, autonomous: Boolean): Wiring`, built from ONE match so the flags and the cell cannot drift. Tiers: - ReadOnly: `--tools read_file,grep,list_dir`, `--no-subagents`, and `--disallowed-tools` for `search_tool,use_tool` (only when no MCP server is attached) plus `ask_user_question` and the scheduler/monitor tools on autonomous turns. Cell Hard. - NetworkOnly: the same plus `web_search,web_fetch`. Cell Hard. - NoTools: `--tools todo_write --disallowed-tools todo_write,search_tool,use_tool,… --no-subagents`. Cell Hard. - Full+All: `--always-approve`. Cell Hard. - Full+Only(_), including the empty set: `--always-approve`. Cell Ignored. - `def enforcementCell(tools, autoApprove, dispatch: TurnDispatch): EnforcementCell`, matching `Fresh | Resumed` exhaustively (resume re-applies the flags). Each rationale cites the flag, `grok 1.0.41`, the probe date and what was observed, like `GeminiArgs`. - `private def allow(names: Seq[String])` must `require(names.nonEmpty)` and only ever receive real tool names. Put the tool-name constants in one place. - `def argv(...)`: `grok --prompt-file

--output-format streaming-messages-json --include-partial-messages --rules `, then `CliArgs.modelArgs` (`-m`/`--model`; `--model` is fine), the session flags, the wiring args, optional `--json-schema `, optional `--agent `, and `--no-auto-update` if the probe task confirmed it. At this stage the session flags come in as a plain parameter (e.g. `sessionFlags: Seq[String]`); the next task adds the `Dispatch[BackendTag.Grok.type]` mapping. - `GrokRefusal`, like claude's `PermissionRefusal`: whole-content match of ``Tool `` was not executed: Denied by permission policy…`` and ``User cancelled the execution for tool `` `` returns the tool name. Quoted text inside longer output must not match. - `GrokDialect`: a `MessagesJsonDialect` value with `backendName = "grok"`, an ask-user matcher that is true only when `name == "use_tool"` and the raw input's `tool_name == "orca__ask_user"` (parse with jsoniter and treat parse failure as false; `search_tool` stays visible), no structured-output tool, `GrokRefusal`, `"unknown"` model mapped to None, and zero usage treated as unobserved. Tests (`grok/src/test/scala/orca/tools/grok/`): - `GrokArgsTest`: every `(ToolSet × AutoApprove shape)` cell. Pin that every ReadOnly/NetworkOnly/NoTools argv has a `--tools` value that is non-empty and contains only known real tool names (never `""`). Also cover mcp=true keeping `search_tool,use_tool`, and optional schema/agent flags. - `GrokRefusalTest`. - A dialect test for the ask-user matcher. Acceptance: `sbt grok/test` is green.

tasks.title: Add BackendTag.Grok, GrokDecoder/GrokTurn/GrokBackend/GrokAgents, and the core flow/runner registration
tasks.description:
Add `Grok` to `enum BackendTag` (`tools/src/main/scala/orca/agents/BackendTag.scala`) and `type GrokAgent = Agent[BackendTag.Grok.type]` beside the others in `tools/src/main/scala/orca/agents/Agent.scala` (~line 419).

In the grok module:
- `GrokArgs`: add `sessionArgs(d: Dispatch[BackendTag.Grok.type])`. `Fresh(Some(id))` renders `--session-id`, `Resume(id, _)` renders `--resume`, and `Fresh(None)` throws `IllegalStateException` because grok is ClientClaimed.
- `GrokTurn.apply(process, openingPrompt, outputSchema, askUser)` over the shared decoder with `GrokDialect`.
- `GrokBackend(cli: CliRunner, grokHome: os.Path = <GROK_HOME env or ~/.grok>, override val workDir: os.Path = os.pwd) extends AgentBackend[BackendTag.Grok.type]`, `private[orca]`:
  - `tag`; `export GrokArgs.enforcementCell`; `structuredOutputMode = RawText`; `cheapModel(_) = Some(GrokModels.BuildFast)`.
  - `sessions = SessionSupport.durable(IdScheme.ClientClaimed, id => …)`, probing `grokHome/"sessions"/URLEncoder.encode(realPath(workDir))/id/"chat_history.jsonl"`. Encode the whole real path, `/` included (`%2Fprivate%2Ftmp%2F…`), and apply whatever non-empty requirement the probe task recorded.
  - `open`: write the prompt with `TurnResources.tempFile(prompt, "orca-grok-prompt-", ".md")`. On interactive turns, `AskUserSession.allocate()` and write a temp `--agent` file (`orca-grok-agent-*.md`) whose frontmatter lists `mcpServers` as a LIST (`- name: orca / type: http / url: <session.server.url> / headers: []`). Compose `--rules` from `SystemPromptComposer.combine(config, Option.when(interactive)(AskUserMcpServer.Hint))`. Build `wiring(config.tools, config.autoApprove, mcp = interactive, autonomous = !interactive)`. Then `SubprocessSpawn.open("grok", events)(cli.spawnPiped(argv, cwd = workDir)) { p => p.closeStdin(); GrokTurn(p, mode.openingPrompt, outputSchema, askUser.fold(AskUserChannel.Unavailable)(AskUserChannel.Mcp(_))) }`.
- `GrokAgents.default(wiring)`: `Agent(backend = new GrokBackend(OsProcCliRunner, workDir = wiring.workDir), config = AgentConfig(model = Some(GrokModels.Default)), …, defaultName = "main")`, plus the `extension (agent: GrokAgent) def fast: GrokAgent = agent.withModel(GrokModels.BuildFast)` tier extension.

Tests:
- `GrokTurnTest` replays each `docs/research/harness-integration/fixtures/grok-*.jsonl` (read via `orca.testkit.RepoRoot.dir`, fed through `FakePipedCliProcess`) and asserts the design-doc §3 outcomes plus `TurnEventConformance.assertGrammar`:
  - write turn: `AgentResult` output, `Usage(fresh 6815, cacheRead 48512, out 566, cost 0.02807, apiCalls 3)`, model `grok-4.7-build-fast`;
  - schema turn: output is the `structured_output` JSON;
  - MCP turn: the `use_tool orca__ask_user` call and its result are suppressed when `askUser` is the Mcp channel, `search_tool` still renders, final text `PINEAPPLE`;
  - dontAsk cancel: `AgentTurnFailed` whose message contains `grok` and `cancelled`, a `ToolDenied("write")` event, and an observed debit;
  - bad model: failure message contains the `errors[]` text, debit Unobserved.
- `GrokBackendTest`, using `SpawnStubCliRunner` like `ClaudeBackendTest`/`GeminiBackendTest`: argv for fresh vs resume, prompt file outside workDir, stdin closed, the `--agent` file on interactive turns with list-form mcpServers, and the probe path encoding.

Core registration, which the new tag forces and without which tests break:
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/settings/AgentSpec.scala`: `harnessNameFor` gets `case BackendTag.Grok => "grok"`.
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/AgentSet.scala`: `def grok: GrokAgent` and the `agentFor` arm; update "five" wording.
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/accessors.scala` and `FlowContext.scala` docs.
- `flow/src/test/.../TestFlowContext.scala`.
- `build.sbt`: runner `dependsOn(grok)`.
- `runner/.../FlowWiring.scala`: `grok` override field.
- `runner/.../WiredAgents.scala`: import, field, `build` arm, "five" wording.
- `runner/.../DefaultFlowContext.scala`: the `export wired.{…}` list.
- `runner/.../flowEntry.scala`: the `flow(...)` `grok` parameter and its pass-through.
- `runner/.../exports.scala`: `GrokAgent` alias, `GrokAgents` and its tier extension.
- `runner/.../EnforcementTableTest.scala`: widen `row(...)` with `grok`, set grok's expected levels (Hard everywhere except Ignored for both Full/Only rows, fresh and resumed), and add `new GrokBackend(cli)` to the backend list. Run it and paste the printed block into AGENTS.md's enforcement table.
- Runner tests that enumerate backends: `RoleAgentsTest` stubs, `LeadAgentIdentityTest`'s match/overrides, `OrcaOverridesTest` if it needs it, `flowtests/FlowCompilesTest.scala`, and `AgentSpecTest` (parse `grok` and `grok:grok-4.7-build-fast`).
- The shell's exhaustive matches, so no `BackendTag` match is left non-exhaustive: `shell/.../sessions/ResumeCommand.scala` gets `case BackendTag.Grok => Right(Seq(binary, "--resume", wireId))`, and `shell/.../create/FlowAuthoring.scala` `slugArgv` gets `Seq(binary, "-m", pin.getOrElse("grok-4.7-build-fast"), "--tools", "todo_write", "--disallowed-tools", "todo_write,search_tool,use_tool", "-p", prompt)`. Add matching cases to `ResumeCommandTest` and `FlowAuthoringTest`.

Acceptance: `sbt test` (full, unit only) is green and the build has no new non-exhaustive-match warnings.

tasks.title: Update README, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING and the other docs for grok
Add a gated GrokIntegrationTest, verify ask_user against orca's McpHost, and run it once
tasks.description:
Add `grok/src/test/scala/orca/tools/grok/GrokIntegrationTest.scala`, mirroring `GeminiIntegrationTest` and `ClaudeIntegrationTest`: gated with `override def munitTests() = if sys.env.contains("ORCA_INTEGRATION") then super.munitTests() else Nil`, a timeout of about 3 minutes, `SupervisedBackend.using(new GrokBackend(OsProcCliRunner, workDir = <temp git repo via orca.testkit.GitRepo/TempDirs>))`, and `model = Model(sys.env.getOrElse("ORCA_GROK_MODEL", "grok-4.7-build-fast"))`. Keep the prompts one line long. Tests:
1. A fresh autonomous turn returns READY with a non-empty wireId equal to the claimed id.
2. Resume recalls a number.
3. A read-only turn asked to create a file and `touch` another leaves the filesystem unchanged. Also run one raw `grok` invocation with the argv `GrokArgs` renders for ReadOnly (or capture the init line via `OpenTurn`/events) and assert that the init `tools` list contains no `write`, `search_replace` or `run_terminal_command`.
4. A structured turn (`outputSchema = Some(<small schema>)`) returns output that parses as that JSON.
5. An interactive turn asks the model to call ask_user. Answer it through the testkit's interaction/`OpenTurn.interactive` path and assert the answer reaches the model. This settles design-doc §11.2 (whether grok's `server/discover` before `initialize` breaks orca's chimp-based `McpHost`). If chimp rejects it fatally, fix it at the seam (e.g. make the grok path tolerate it, or document it) and record what happened.

The re-claim refusal is optional (claude covers it via `SessionSupport.heldClaim`); include it only if it is one extra call.

Run it once in the foreground: `ORCA_INTEGRATION=1 sbt "grok/testOnly orca.tools.grok.GrokIntegrationTest"`. Report the actual outcome. If a test fails because of grok behaviour, fix the seam with a unit test pinning the observed shape before re-running at most once more.

Then update `INTEGRATE_GROK_BUILD.md`: mark §6's `server/discover` item, the stricter-tier resume, the web/read-only items you observed, and the integration results as **[verified grok 1.0.41, 2026-09-27, Linux]**. Refresh §11 so it lists only what is still open (pricing rows as a TODO, ACP/interactive approvals). Also note the implementation status (module and files) at the top.

resultJson.brief:
## Ground rules
- Read CLAUDE.md, then AGENTS.md (invariants, vocabulary) and CONTRIBUTING.md (build/test).
- Invoke the `direct-style-scala` skill before writing or reviewing any Scala.
- No class-level `var`s. New mutable state requires CLAUDE.md's research + critique agents; the design needs none: decoders are pure folds over immutable `State`.
- Recoverable failures are `Either[E <: OrcaFlowException, T]`. Failures before spawn throw `OrcaFlowException`; after the turn ran they surface as `AgentTurnFailed` via `Settled.Failed`.
- No defaults on persisted or domain fields.
- scalacOptions include `-Wunused:all -Wvalue-discard -Wnonunit-statement`. Non-exhaustive matches only warn, but `AgentSpec.harnessNames`, `WiredAgents.byTag` and `EnforcementTableTest` iterate `BackendTag.values`, so a missing arm is a runtime MatchError or test failure.
- Tests use munit (`munit.FunSuite`), forked JVMs, and live in `<module>/src/test/scala/...` with the same package.
- Don't push or open PRs. Don't invent pricing rates.

## Design sources (follow them, don't re-derive)
- `INTEGRATE_GROK_BUILD.md`:
  - §2 invocation; §3 wire differences; §4 sessions; §5 tier flags and the empty-`--tools` trap; §6 `--agent` file for ask_user (mcpServers must be a YAML LIST); §7 models; §8 shell resume/slug; §9 enforcement row; §10 code sketch; §11 open questions.
  - Update its verified markers as you go.
- `HARNESS_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md`: §2 the AgentBackend contract, §4 LineDecoder, §7 registration checklist, §8 testing.
- Fixtures in `docs/research/harness-integration/fixtures/`: `grok-write.jsonl`, `grok-schema.jsonl`, `grok-mcp.jsonl`, `grok-dontask-cancel.jsonl`, `grok-badmodel.jsonl` (grok 1.0.41). The README there describes each. In tests, read them via `orca.testkit.RepoRoot.dir / "docs/research/harness-integration/fixtures/..."`.
- `grok-badmodel.jsonl` shows: init `model:"nope-model"`, `tools:[]`; result `is_error:true`, `subtype:error_during_execution`, all-zero usage with `server_tool_use:{web_search_requests:0}`, `total_cost_usd:0.0`, `errors:[...]`, no top-level `model`.

## Modules
- `tools` (`orca-tools`) holds the SPI:
  - `orca.backend.{AgentBackend, LineDecoder, Step, Settled, DecodedTurn, DecodedTurnSpec, StreamSource, TurnEvent, AgentResult, AskUserChannel, AskUserEchoes, SessionSupport, IdScheme, Dispatch, SubprocessSpawn, SystemPromptComposer, TurnResources, CliArgs, TurnRequest, TurnMode}`;
  - `orca.backend.mcp.{AskUserMcpServer, AskUserSession, McpHost}` (chimp-server over tapir netty; McpHost binds 127.0.0.1:0/mcp);
  - `orca.agents.{BackendTag, Agent, AgentConfig, ToolSet, AutoApprove, Enforcement, EnforcementCell, TurnDispatch, StructuredOutputMode, Model, SessionId, WireSessionId}`;
  - `orca.events.{Usage, TurnDebit}`.
  - The new shared decoder goes in `tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/messagesjson/`.
- `claude`: the current owner of the stream-json code:
  - `claude/src/main/scala/orca/tools/claude/ClaudeDecoder.scala` has `ClaudeDecoder(outputSchema) extends LineDecoder[BackendTag.ClaudeCode.type, State]` with `State(initModel, deltasSinceLastFullMessage, responseIds, echoes)` and `ClaudeTurn.apply(process, openingPrompt, outputSchema, askUser)`;
  - `streamjson/{InboundMessage, ContentBlock, StreamEventPayload, OutboundMessage}.scala`;
  - `PermissionRefusal.scala`;
  - `ClaudeBackend.scala` has `AskUserToolName = "mcp__orca__ask_user"`, `StructuredOutputToolName = "StructuredOutput"`, and the `cwdSlug` probe;
  - tests are `ClaudeTurnTest`, `ClaudeBackendTest`, `streamjson/*Test`, `PermissionRefusalTest`, `ClaudeIntegrationTest`.
- `gemini`: the closest template for file layout. `GeminiBackend.scala` shows `open` and `SubprocessSpawn` usage, and `GeminiArgs.scala` shows the `ApprovalWiring(args, cell)` one-match pattern and the rationale style. Also see `GeminiAgents.scala`, `GeminiModels.scala`, and `GeminiIntegrationTest.scala` for the gating pattern.
- `flow`: `orca/settings/AgentSpec.scala` (`harnessNameFor`), `orca/AgentSet.scala` (`def <name>`, `agentFor`), `orca/accessors.scala`, `orca/FlowContext.scala`, `orca/events/Pricing.scala`; tests `TestFlowContext.scala` and `settings/AgentSpecTest.scala`.
- `runner`:
  - `orca/runner/{FlowWiring, WiredAgents, DefaultFlowContext}.scala`, `orca/flowEntry.scala`, `orca/exports.scala`, `orca/runner/terminal/ReadOnlyTools.scala`;
  - tests `EnforcementTableTest` (renders the AGENTS.md block; paste on failure), `RoleAgentsTest`, `LeadAgentIdentityTest`, `DefaultModelsPricedTest`, `OrcaOverridesTest`, `flowtests/FlowCompilesTest`.
- `shell`:
  - `sessions/ResumeCommand.scala` builds the binary name from `AgentSpec.harnessNameFor`; grok's settings name equals its binary;
  - `create/FlowAuthoring.scala` `slugArgv`;
  - `wizard/{ModelCatalog, Wizard}.scala`;
  - `actions/SettingsEditAction.scala:30`;
  - tests `ResumeCommandTest`, `FlowAuthoringTest`, `WizardTest`.
- `build.sbt`: modules follow the same shape (`lazy val gemini = (project in file("gemini")).dependsOn(tools, tools % "test->test").settings(commonSettings).settings(name := "orca-gemini", libraryDependencies ++= Seq(osLib, jsoniter, jsoniterMacros))`). The runner `dependsOn` list and the root `.aggregate(...)` must include the new module.

## Key APIs
- `LineDecoder[B, S]`: `backendName`, `terminalMessageNoun`, `init`, `line(state, line): Step[B,S]`, `failedTurnDebit(state)`. Use `Step.continue(state, events*)`, `Step.Continue(state, list)` and `Step.Settle(state, events, Settled.Succeeded(AgentResult[B](WireSessionId(id), output, usage, model)) | Settled.Failed(msg, TurnDebit))`. A throw inside `line` becomes a parse-error event, so parse with Unknown fallbacks.
- `DecodedTurn.start(StreamSource.fromProcess(p), DecodedTurnSpec(openingPrompt, outputSchema, askUser), decoder)(using Ox): LiveTurn[B]`.
- `AskUserEchoes`: `suppress(id)` on the call, `consume(id): Option[AskUserEchoes]` on the result.
- `SessionSupport.durable(IdScheme.ClientClaimed, probe: String => Boolean)`. The probe must be side-effect free; a throw reads as "gone".
- `Dispatch[B]`: `Fresh(claim: Option[WireSessionId[B]])` and `Resume(wireId, origin)`. `WireSessionId.value(id)`, `SessionId.fresh[B]`.
- `SubprocessSpawn.open(label, turn.events)(cli.spawnPiped(args, cwd = workDir))(process => …)`.
- `TurnResources.tempFile(contents, prefix, suffix)(using ResourceScope)` writes under $TMPDIR, never inside workDir.
- `SystemPromptComposer.combine(config, extraHint: Option[String])`. `AskUserMcpServer.Hint`; `AskUserSession.allocate()` gives `.server.url`.
- `CliArgs.flag(name, opt)(render)` and `CliArgs.modelArgs(config)` (`--model`).
- `EnforcementCell(Enforcement.Hard|SandboxApprox|PromptOnly|Ignored, rationale)`.
- `Usage(freshInputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, cacheWriteInputTokens, outputTokens, reasoningOutputTokens, cost, apiCalls)`, constructed by name; also `Usage.empty` and `usage.spentTokens`. `TurnDebit.Observed(usage, model)` and `TurnDebit.Unobserved`. `Pricing.resolve` already treats a reported 0 cost against spent tokens as no report.

## Test helpers (tools test->test)
- `orca.subprocess.{FakePipedCliProcess (enqueueStdout/closeStdout/closeStderr), SpawnStubCliRunner, StubCliRunner}`.
- `orca.backend.{TurnEventConformance.assertGrammar(events, completedNormally), SupervisedBackend.using(backend)(body)}`.
- `orca.testkit.{OpenTurn.interactive, TempDirs.dir(), GitRepo, RepoRoot, TestAgent, ScriptedBackend, Usages.usage}`.
- Turn tests wrap bodies in `supervised` (see `ClaudeTurnTest.liveTest`).

## Non-obvious facts
- Grok's MCP tools arrive via meta-tools: the call is `tool_use{name:"use_tool", input:{tool_name:"orca__ask_user",…}}`, so the ask-user matcher needs the raw input as well as the name. The model may call `search_tool` first; that call renders.
- Grok has no injected StructuredOutput tool. Under `--json-schema` every text block is JSON and the value is in `result.structured_output` (the decoder already prefers it). Use `StructuredOutputMode.RawText`.
- `result` has no top-level `model`; the decoder falls back to `init.model`.
- An empty `--tools ""` or unknown-only `--tools` DISABLES filtering. NoTools therefore names `todo_write` and then disallows it.
- Headless grok defaults to bypassPermissions, so every tier needs explicit flags.
- The session probe path is `$GROK_HOME|~/.grok /sessions/<URL-encoded REAL path of workDir, '/' → %2F>/<id>/chat_history.jsonl`. Watch `/tmp` → `/private/tmp` on macOS.
- Re-claiming an existing `--session-id` errors with "already in use"; `SessionSupport.heldClaim` already handles that.
- SIGINT kills grok immediately.
- Enforcement row: every tier Hard except both `Full, Only(_)` / `Only()` rows, which are Ignored. Resumed turns are classified the same as fresh ones.
- Live grok calls cost money. Always use `-m grok-4.7-build-fast`, one-line prompts, and a handful of calls in total.
